fields.meta_title: Employee Onboarding Workflow: Offer to Day 30 | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an employee onboarding workflow that chases unsigned forms before the start date and checks in with every new hire on day 30.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Onboarding Workflow From Offer to Day 30
fields.hero_description: Build an employee onboarding workflow that gives each new hire's tasks an owner and a due date, from offer to day 30.
fields.features_subheading: Each new hire gets one record that holds every task, its owner, and its due date.
fields.feature_1:
A record the day the offer is accepted

The app reads your HR system through its API and opens an onboarding record when a candidate accepts. The record starts with the role and start date from the signed offer.
fields.feature_2:
Tasks routed to the team that owns them

IT, facilities, and payroll each get a task list for the new hire. Tell Emergent which tasks belong to which role, and a warehouse hire gets a different list than an engineer.
fields.feature_3:
Forms signed before day one

The new hire opens one link, fills in each form, and signs on screen. The app captures each e-signature and marks that form done on the new hire's record for HR to see.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders before anything runs late

Every task has a due date counted from the start date. The app reminds the owner by email or Slack on the days you pick, then alerts a named person if the task stays open.
fields.feature_5:
A live board of every hire in progress

HR sees each new hire by stage and start date, with any overdue task at the top. The board updates the moment IT or payroll marks its task done in the onboarding app.
fields.feature_6:
The onboarding app's code in GitHub

Export the full code of the app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Anyone on your team can review how employee records are stored and change the app like any other code.

fields.usecase_heading: Where a New Hire's First Month Slips
fields.tab_content_1:
HR hears about any unsigned form 3 days before the start

Delphine Arceneaux accepts a front desk role at Oakhurst Pediatrics, and the app sends her 5 forms to sign online. She signs 4 of the 5 and gets an email reminder every 2 days about the handbook acknowledgment. Three days before her start date, the HR coordinator, Renata Szabo, gets a direct message naming it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Four teams get day-one tasks when the offer is accepted

Amadou Fairweather accepts a dispatcher role at Kestrel Ridge Logistics, and the app opens a task for each of 4 teams, due 2 business days before his Monday start. Three of the 4 are done. The badge is still open, and the facilities lead, Gwendolyn Marsh, gets a direct message about it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Solo shifts open only after all 4 courses

Thornbury Outdoor Supply gives every new store associate 4 required courses to finish by day 14. On day 14, Paloma Reinholt has finished 3 of the 4, and the returns process course is still open. The app keeps her solo shifts locked and tells the store manager, Corwin Ashby, which course she has left.
fields.tab_content_4:
HR partners see every day-30 score under 3

On day 30, Yusuf Abernathy answers 3 questions about his first month at Fallowmere Software. He rates getting help at 2 out of 5 and writes that nobody has shown him who approves code reviews. Any score under 3 goes to the HR partner, Saoirse Kettering, as a direct message with his comment.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan an employee onboarding workflow and its reminders, then build it with Emergent and test it on a past hire.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose the event that starts it
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every task between the accepted offer and day 30, such as signed forms or a first-week training plan. Next to each task, note who does it today and what it waits on.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Assign every task to a team or a named role, such as IT for the laptop or the hiring manager for the first-week schedule. Keep separate lists where roles differ, since a warehouse hire and an engineer need different equipment.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose the one event that opens a new hire's record, such as an offer marked accepted in your applicant tracking system. Count every due date from the start date on that record.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide how many days before the start date each task is due, how often its owner gets a reminder, and who hears about it when it runs late. Write those numbers next to each task.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the workflow in a prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the task lists and day counts in plain English, the way you would brief a new HR coordinator. Emergent builds the onboarding app from that prompt, with the employee record, forms, reminders, and the board.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the tools you already use
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect your HR system and Slack through their APIs. Each new hire then arrives with the start date and manager filled in, and alerts reach people in the tools they already check.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it on one past hire
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run one recent hire through the app with their real offer and start dates. Check that each reminder lands on the day you planned, then adjust the day counts before the next offer goes out.

faq_plan.q: What is an employee onboarding workflow?
faq_plan.a: An employee onboarding workflow is the set of tasks a company runs between an accepted offer and a new hire who can do the job. Each task is assigned to a person and tied to a date. SHRM defines onboarding as the process of integrating new employees into an organization. The workflow is the part of that process you can schedule and track.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an employee onboarding workflow?
faq_plan.a: Write the workflow down before you build anything. For each role you hire, list every task through day 30, who owns it, and the day it is due counted from the start date. Then describe those lists in a prompt in Emergent's AI automation builder. Emergent builds the onboarding app with its database and dashboard, and you change it later by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: Which tasks in an HR onboarding workflow belong to HR and which to the hiring manager?
faq_plan.a: Give HR the paperwork and the check-ins that compare one hire with another. Give the hiring manager the job itself, such as the first-week schedule and the first real assignment. Write the owner next to every task, because a task each side thinks the other has is the one that slips.

faq_plan.q: How can AI agents automate an employee onboarding workflow?
faq_plan.hint: How to use AI agents to automate employee onboarding workflows?
faq_plan.a: AI agents fit the reading and chasing, not the decisions. An AI step can read an uploaded form into fields on the employee record and send any field it is unsure of to a person. Keep judgment calls, such as a missed training deadline, with a manager. Recruitment automation uses the same split earlier in hiring, where software handles scheduling and people make the offer.

faq_plan.q: What should an employee onboarding workflow finish before the first day?
faq_plan.a: Paperwork, equipment, and accounts should all be finished before day one. Send the forms as soon as the candidate accepts, and open the laptop and account tasks for each team at the same time. Set those due dates 2 business days before the start to leave room for a late delivery. A few days out, send the new hire a short note with where to go and who will meet them.

faq_plan.q: How long should an employee onboarding workflow run?
faq_plan.a: Build the tasks around the first 30 days, then keep check-ins running after that. Setup and required training belong in that first month. For roles that take longer to learn, add check-ins at day 60 and day 90. Close the workflow when the new hire and the manager both say the role is clear, and record that date on the employee's record.

faq_plan.q: How does an employee onboarding workflow record who finished each task?
faq_plan.a: It logs every task change on the employee's record with the name of the person who made it and the time. In an app built with Emergent, that history is stored in a database you own, next to the rest of the employee data. If an audit workflow already runs for other processes, point it at the same log instead of keeping a second copy.

faq_plan.q: Can one employee onboarding workflow cover remote and office hires?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep one workflow and add a work-location field that switches a few tasks. A remote hire's laptop ships to a home address with a delivery date before the start, while an office hire gets a desk and a badge instead. The first-week schedule lists video call links in place of room numbers. The forms and the check-ins stay the same for both.

faq_plan.q: What happens to an employee onboarding workflow when a start date changes?
faq_plan.a: Every due date should move with it. Store each due date as an offset from the start, such as day 14, instead of a calendar date. When HR changes the start date, the app recalculates each task and alerts every owner whose deadline moved. When Emergent builds the app, those alerts can go out by Slack, email, or in-app. If an offer is withdrawn, close the open tasks.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep the documents in an employee onboarding workflow up to date?
faq_plan.a: Give each document and course an owner and a review date, and keep both on the list the workflow reads from. When a policy changes, the owner updates the file once, and every new hire after that date gets the new version. If your handbook needs sign-off from leadership before it goes out, run its edits through a content workflow with a review step.

plan.angle: The top 10 are HR blog checklists and 30-60-90 explainers that list onboarding steps but never show them running. This page treats onboarding as a workflow with owners and deadlines from the accepted offer to day 30, then shows the app running four stages for four employers: signed forms before the start date, day-one tasks fanned out to four teams, required courses that gate solo shifts, and a day-30 pulse that reaches HR. The FAQ answers builder questions on owners, AI agents, the first day, length, records, remote hires, start-date changes and keeping content current, and leaves hiring itself to the recruitment automation page.
